name: Dmitriy Zaporozhets
milestone_by_age_26: Created the open-source GitLab project from Ukraine in October 2011 (with Valery Sizov) as a self-hosted Git collaboration tool while working as a web developer, at about age 24; later co-founded GitLab Inc. with Sid Sijbrandij.
early_history_summary: Dmitriy (Dmytro) Zaporozhets studied at Kharkiv National Automobile and Highway University with interest in software engineering and worked as a web developer at Sphere Software in Ukraine. Frustrated by the lack of modern open-source self-hosted Git tooling, he built GitLab as a hobby project in October 2011. Sid Sijbrandij later commercialized the project; Zaporozhets joined full-time as CTO around 2013 and remained through GitLab's 2021 IPO before stepping down as Engineering Fellow.
family_context_summary: Worked from a rural Ukrainian house without running water while starting GitLab; family financial details otherwise not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: open source, Git, Ukraine, self-hosted DevOps, co-founder Sid Sijbrandij, adversity, domain immersion
evidence_summary: Kyiv Post reported Zaporozhets as 29 in January 2017 (implying birth around 1987–88, correcting the batch CSV's 1984), and Forbes listed him on 30 Under 30 Enterprise Technology. Multiple primary sources (GitLab farewell blog, handbook history, Kyiv Post) confirm he started GitLab in October 2011 from Ukraine as a hobby while employed as a developer, well before age 26. Advantages were mainly direct developer-problem immersion, open-source distribution, and constraint-driven building rather than elite institutions or family capital.
starting_point: Ukrainian developer from the Kharkiv area; early GitLab work was done from a country house without running water while employed at a local software firm.
current_position: Co-founder of GitLab; left Engineering Fellow role at GitLab Inc. in 2021 after the company's IPO; creator of the original GitLab open-source project.

trajectory.event: Created the open-source GitLab project in October with Valery Sizov while working as a Ukrainian web developer.
Joined GitLab full-time (initially without formal title, later CTO) to commercialize the open-source product with Sid Sijbrandij.
GitLab participated in Y Combinator (W15), accelerating company growth and fundraising.
Transitioned from CTO to Engineering Fellow as the company scaled beyond a coding CTO role.
Attended GitLab's Nasdaq listing and stepped down from Engineering Fellow after a planned 10-year commitment.

early_history_summary: Ockerbloom attended Carnegie Mellon University in the 1990s, earning a PhD in computer science. In 1993 he began The Online Books Page, a major free online books index, and in 1994 created Banned Books On-Line in response to campus Usenet censorship. He later became a digital library architect/planner at the University of Pennsylvania and has been active on copyright and open-access issues.

name: Amitt Mahajan
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded MyMiniLife (2007) and, after Zynga's mid-2009 acquisition, co-created/led engineering for FarmVille (launched June 2009), which rapidly became Facebook's leading social game—while under 30 on Forbes 30 Under 30 (2012) and a 2006 UIUC CS graduate, placing the FarmVille milestone at about age 24–25.
early_history_summary: Amitt Mahajan earned a BS in Computer Science from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (class of 2006), graduating early and joining Epic Games to work on Unreal Engine 3 tools and Gears of War. In 2007 he co-founded MyMiniLife with fellow Illinois alumni; Zynga acquired the company in 2009 and used its stack for FarmVille, which Mahajan led as director of engineering. He later was CTO of Zynga Japan, founded Red Hot Labs, co-founded Presence Capital, and founded Proof of Play.
family_context_summary: Not documented in detail in reviewed sources; has written publicly about interviewing his mother later in life.
primary_early_advantage_tags: UIUC, Epic Games, Facebook platform, FarmVille, MyMiniLife, Zynga, co-founders
evidence_summary: UIUC alumni sources document BS '06, Epic Games work, 2007 MyMiniLife founding, and Zynga/FarmVille engineering leadership. Zynga Wikipedia and contemporary press date the MyMiniLife acquisition and FarmVille launch to mid-2009. Forbes 30 Under 30 (2012) implies he was still under 30 then, so FarmVille occurred by about age 25. Early advantages include elite CS pipeline, peer cofounders, Facebook distribution wave, and deep game-engineering immersion rather than documented family wealth.
starting_point: Computer science graduate of UIUC (BS 2006); early professional start at Epic Games; family background not detailed in reviewed sources.
current_position: Founder/CEO of Proof of Play (onchain games, e.g. Pirate Nation); serial entrepreneur and investor; co-creator of FarmVille; former Zynga engineering leader.

trajectory.event: Graduated early with a BS in Computer Science from UIUC and joined Epic Games working on Unreal Engine 3 tools and Gears of War.
Co-founded MyMiniLife with Illinois classmates, building a virtual-world creation platform.
MyMiniLife acquired by Zynga; co-created and led engineering for FarmVille, which scaled to tens of millions of Facebook users.

Co-founded Presence Capital focused on VR/AR early-stage investing after prior exits including Toro to Google.
Founded Proof of Play to build fully onchain games, launching titles such as Pirate Nation.

name: Adrian Carmack
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded id Software on February 1, 1991 at age 21 with John Carmack, John Romero, and Tom Hall after meeting at Softdisk; as lead artist shipped Commander Keen (1990–91), Wolfenstein 3D (1992, age 23), and Doom (December 1993, age 24), defining the studio's gore aesthetic and the term 'gibs'.
early_history_summary: Adrian Carmack (no relation to John Carmack) applied for a Softdisk Gamer's Edge internship around age 21, standing out with long hair and metal shirts. He moonlighted with the team on early titles and left Softdisk to co-found id Software in early 1991. His dark, gory art direction on Wolfenstein 3D and Doom became culturally definitive; he held a large ownership stake until leaving in 2005 amid a dispute over a forced buyout.
family_context_summary: Not richly documented in reviewed sources; early work experience included hospital communications aide duties where he saw emergency-room imagery that later informed Doom's visceral style (per Masters of Doom).
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as a games-industry family; domain craft appears self-developed and peer-forged at Softdisk/id.
primary_early_advantage_tags: id Software, Softdisk, John Carmack, John Romero, Tom Hall, shareware, FPS wave, Doom art
evidence_summary: Wikipedia, DoomWiki, and Masters of Doom-aligned secondary sources confirm birth May 5, 1969, Softdisk origins, id founding February 1991 (age 21), and art leadership on Wolfenstein 3D and Doom before age 25. Primary leverage was an exceptional cofounder team riding the PC shareware and FPS technology wave, plus scarce art specialization, not inherited capital or elite schooling.
starting_point: American artist who entered games via a Softdisk internship around age 21; not from a documented industry family dynasty.
current_position: Former id Software co-founder and major shareholder (left 2005); later owner of Ireland's Heritage Golf & Spa Resort; reunited with Romero on Night Work Games / Blackroom project.

trajectory.event: Joined Softdisk's Gamer's Edge art effort and collaborated with Romero, John Carmack, and Tom Hall on early PC games.
Co-founded id Software (February 1) and shipped Commander Keen shareware titles as company artist.
Art-directed Wolfenstein 3D, a breakthrough commercial first-person shooter released on his 23rd birthday (May 5, 1992).
Created Doom's signature grotesque aesthetic and 'gibs' visual language for the genre-defining December 1993 release.
Continued as id artist through Quake's launch as the studio pushed fully 3D FPS technology.
Left id Software after a dispute over a forced sale of his large ownership stake; later sued former partners.
Reunited with John Romero under Night Work Games to announce the FPS Blackroom Kickstarter (later paused).

name: James F. Allen
milestone_by_age_26: Born 1950; PhD from University of Toronto in 1979 at about age 29 under C. Raymond Perrault. early_history_summary: James Frederick Allen is a computational linguist known for Allen's interval algebra and natural language understanding systems (TRIPS, PLOW). After a 1979 Toronto PhD he joined University of Rochester faculty, later serving as department chair, editor-in-chief of Computational Linguistics (1983–1993), AAAI founding fellow (1990), and associate director at IHMC.
evidence_summary: Standard academic biography places birth in 1950 and the doctoral milestone in 1979 (~age 29). No undergraduate or pre-26 research awards or publications with firm dates establishing a material age-26 milestone were found.
